title: Integration boarding surge playbook notes — BlueHarbor rapid onboarding (2026-12-20)
content:
Context:
This doc captures the Dec 20 2026 joint sync between Solutions Engineering and Professional Services to align the surge playbook for BlueHarbor: a large retail customer that wants production traffic within 4 weeks. Notes are intentionally practical — immediate runbook items, short-term risk mitigations, and a minimal rollout checklist for a fast but safe delivery.

Attendees:
- Aisha Patel (SE lead)
- Ethan Shaw (ProServices PM)
- María González (SRE)
- Liam O'Connell (Integrations Eng)
- Priya Menon (Security / Compliance)
- Guest: BlueHarbor technical lead (via teleconf)

Meeting goals:
1) Agree on a prioritized surge checklist for week 0-2 to enable Canary traffic.
2) Identify top-3 blockers and owners for immediate escalations.
3) Define fallback policy (model + capacity) in case of latency or accuracy regressions.

Summary of decisions:
- We will run a staged Canary: 1% traffic day 1, 10% day 3, 50% day 8 if no regressions. Canary traffic will be routed to a dedicated Dedicated cluster (reserved capacity) with autoscale cap set to 2x baseline. (Owner: Aisha)
- Model pin: BlueHarbor requests pinned model variant rwd-13B-quant-v2 for consistency. We will keep a lighter fallback rwd-7B-fp16 in routing policies. (Owner: Liam)
- KMS integration: BlueHarbor requires customer-managed KMS for embeddings storage. Security will verify key rotation policy and CORS rules before ship.  (Owner: Priya)

Top blockers (immediate):
1) Firewall/NAT routing: BlueHarbor's egress NAT mapping conflicts with our IP allowlist automation. Impact: blocks webhook callbacks for job completions. Action: Ethan to coordinate with BlueHarbor netops and get CIDR exceptions by 2026-12-23. (Ethan)
2) Latency spike in long-context prompts: observed 2.2x p95 for 8k token workloads on local sims. Action: María will run a profiling pass and enable adaptive batching with a 50ms window for the Canary cluster by 2026-12-22. (María)
3) Auth token exchange TTL mismatch between BlueHarbor session manager and Redwood token service. Action: Liam to add a short-lived shim to refresh tokens and backfill logs for three days. Deployment target 2026-12-24. (Liam)

Playbook: Week-by-week runbook (condensed)
- Week 0 (setup, day -2..0):
  - Reserve Dedicated cluster (2x baseline) and attach VPC peering. (Aisha)
  - Share onboarding checklist with BlueHarbor: routing table, cert thumbprints, IP ranges. (Ethan)
  - Confirm KMS key policy and generate test encrypt/decrypt vectors. (Priya)
  - Create Canary monitor dashboard in Console: token-level cost, p50/p95 latency, top error codes. (María)

- Week 1 (Canary day 1..7):
  - Day 1: 1% traffic routed. Run synthetic correctness eval suite (20 canonical prompts). Stop if BLEU/ROUGE drops > 6% or accuracy on intent test drops > 4%. (Aisha + María)
  - Day 3: 10% traffic if stability OK. Run cold-start latency tests and KV cache hit-rate checks. (María)
  - Daily standup: 09:30 PST, 15 min rapid ops notes. (All)

- Week 2 (broadening):
  - Increment to 50% by day 8 if no regressions. Enable autoscale burst up to 3x for peak windows. (Aisha)
  - Validate logs retention and PII redaction paths for sample request set. (Priya)
  - Begin run-rate egress billing estimate and send to finance for provisional PO. (Ethan)

Operational controls and fallbacks:
- Fallback model policy: route to rwd-7B-fp16 when p95 latency > 1.8s for 3 consecutive 5-min windows OR error rate > 0.6%. (María)
- Circuit-breaker: auto-throttle client to 10 rps when KV cache miss rate > 30% and latency trend upward. (Liam)
- Observability: set regression alert tied to eval set (Confluence:blueharbor-rapid-onboard-v1) and add an on-call rotation for first 14 days. (María + Ethan)

Safety and compliance checks:
- Data residency: BlueHarbor requires EU data paths for specific datasets. We will ensure embeddings are stored in eu-central-1 and tag requests accordingly. (Priya)
- Audit trail: enable request-level audit logging for the Dedicated cluster with 90-day retention. Confirm storage encryption status with ops. (Priya)

Open questions / unresolved:
- BlueHarbor L2 wants a formal SLO for 99th percentile token latency — need legal sign-off if we commit. (Next: Sales + Legal sync by 2026-12-22)
- Is there appetite for a staged quantization trial to reduce cost? Customer deferred to post-GoLive. (Action: Aisha to schedule a post-mortem + quantization proposal)

Action items (owner, due):
- Ethan: Obtain BlueHarbor netops CIDRs and update allowlist automation (2026-12-23).
- María: Profiling run and adaptive batching config for Canary cluster (2026-12-22).
- Liam: Implement token refresh shim & logging backfill (2026-12-24).
- Priya: Finalize KMS policy verification + audit log encryption check (2026-12-23).
- Aisha: Provision Dedicated cluster and create Canary dashboards (2026-12-21).
- Ethan + Finance: Draft provisional PO and run-rate estimate (2026-12-25).

Quick retrospective notes from the session:
- What went well: cross-team clarity on immediate blockers, concise Canary thresholds agreed.
- What needs improving: earlier network discovery — we lost 48 hours clarifying NAT details. For future surges, add a preflight network questionnaire to the intake form. (Owner: Ethan)

Next meeting:
- Rapid surge check-in: 2026-12-22 09:30 PST (15 min). Agenda: unblockers status, Canary readiness check, any urgent customer asks.
